plan_a_advantages: Lower overall training volume, potentially reducing risk of overtraining.
More frequent easy runs could aid in maintaining a consistent running base.
plan_b_advantages: Includes threshold and hill work, directly targeting speed and climbing strength.
Longer run incorporates a controlled aerobic effort, building endurance relevant to trail races.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more structured, intensity-based workouts like threshold runs and hill sessions, which directly address the goal of improving speed and climbing ability – crucial elements of trail running. Plan A, conversely, focuses almost exclusively on easy runs, which, while beneficial for recovery and consistency, won't provide the stimulus needed for significant speed gains. While Plan A prioritizes low-impact recovery, Plan B’s inclusion of harder sessions will lead to greater adaptations and ultimately, faster times.
